solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Greek character's in charge of booze for the party

parts.note: MU is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and the 's stands for 'is', giving S
ale is a kind of booze

explanation.surface: A Greek man in charge of the drinks for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Greek character' is read as 'is' and supplies an S.
explanation.definitionFit: A musicale is a social gathering built around a musical performance, a kind of party.

clue.text: Mark, son of Ronald in Glasgow?

parts.note: Mac in Scottish Gaelic surnames means son of, apt for Glasgow
Ron is the short form of the name Ronald

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Glaswegian called Mark is the son of a man named Ronald.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Glasgow?' tells you to use the Scottish prefix: Mac means 'son of' in Scottish surnames, so MacRon is 'son of Ron'.
explanation.definitionFit: A macron is a diacritical mark, a short bar placed over a vowel to show it is long.

clue.text: Remark about young louse makes sense

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to say something is to remark it
a nit is the egg or young of a louse

explanation.surface: A comment about head lice turns out to be quite reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal: the louse goes inside the remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanity is soundness of mind, good sense, as in 'a voice of sanity'.

clue.text: Carry on and on getting money when given external psychological stimulus

indicators.note: external says the stimulus word sits on the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: a cue is a signal or stimulus prompting a response
taken as written
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going on and on about money when prompted by a psychological trigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'external' says the stimulus wraps round the rest. TIN is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue is to carry on, keep going without stopping.

clue.text: General so so silly to get very angry

indicators.note: silly suggests these letters are being foolishly jumbled up

parts.note: taken as written, both words used

explanation.surface: A mediocre general so foolish that he flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges GENERAL plus SO SO. LOSE ONE'S RAG is a British idiom for losing your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's rag is an informal British idiom for becoming furious, flying off the handle.

clue.text: After dull work get a nervous disorder

parts.note: a chore is a tedious, routine task

explanation.surface: Boring work gives someone a bad case of nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Chorea is a neurological condition causing jerky involuntary movements, such as Huntington's chorea.

clue.text: Acclaimed hospital first class — showed the way to go

parts.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
A1 means first class, written AI in crosswords
to lead is to show the way, past tense led

explanation.surface: A top-class hospital is praised for pioneering the way forward.
explanation.walkthrough: AI is A1, 'first class', with the 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to acclaim them, as in a player hailed as a genius.

clue.text: Sail, trailing at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sail dragging behind a ship out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges TRAILING.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringtail is a small extra sail set abaft the spanker or gaff sail on a ship.

clue.text: A cold minister sticking to the truth

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a curate is a minister of the church, an assistant to a vicar

explanation.surface: A chilly clergyman who refuses to tell lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct and faithful to the facts, true to them.

clue.text: Soon is in church to turn into a saint

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
anon is an old word for soon, shortly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soon someone in church will be made a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal: the church abbreviation is the outer piece. 'Soon' uses an archaic word, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To canonise is formally to declare a dead person a saint.

clue.text: It involves carting round a hamper? Easy task!

definitions.text: It involves carting round a hamper?
definitions.meaning: an outdoor meal where food is carried in a basket

explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is an outdoor meal often carried in a hamper, and informally a very easy task.

clue.text: Rustic bench in a grand estate?

parts.note: country, as an adjective, means rustic or rural
a bench is a kind of seat

explanation.surface: A rural bench sitting in the grounds of a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: A country seat is a large country house with its land, a grand estate of the gentry.

clue.text: Get-up could get you dismissed with tantrum following

parts.note: a batter dismissed in cricket is out
a fit is a sudden outburst, such as a fit of temper

explanation.surface: A batter given out throws a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT is the cricket term for a batter who has been dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-up is an informal word for a set of clothes, a costume or ensemble.

clue.text: Confused oldster clings on to a guide

indicators.note: clings on to means holding something within its grasp, so it contains the next piece
confused says the letters of the old person are muddled

explanation.surface: A muddled old man hangs on to someone leading him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges OLDSTER to LODESTR, and 'clings on to' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestar is a star used to steer by, and figuratively a guiding principle or guide.

clue.text: See 4
What could be trio behaving in unrestrained fashion

parts.note: read the phrase backwards as wordplay: the second word is the anagram of trio, and the first word is an anagram indicator

explanation.surface: Musicians performing with wild abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer itself is wordplay, an anagram indicator followed by a word whose letters rearranged spell 'trio'.
explanation.definitionFit: Running riot means acting wildly and without restraint.

clue.text: See 15
Rogue American President — liar ultimately with verbal onslaught

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, a US President

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word liar

parts.note: a rant is a long angry outburst of words

explanation.surface: A crooked US president, a liar, unleashes a tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes R, the last letter of 'liar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogue as an adjective means deviant or abnormal, straying from the norm.

clue.text: Short hint given to cleaner: members will want to come in here

definitions.text: members will want to come in here

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a clue is a hint
a broom is a cleaning implement

explanation.surface: A brief tip passed on to a cleaner about where club members will be coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts the last letter from CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A clubroom is a room set aside for a club, which its members enter.

clue.text: A person posting a letter, we hear — someone coming up the hill?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the spoken form of the phrase is what counts

parts.note: one who sends a letter is a sender

explanation.surface: Someone posting a letter is climbing up a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' asks for the sound: 'a sender' is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascender is one who climbs or goes up, such as someone walking up a slope.

clue.text: Nasty slob 'ad money, becoming very cheeky

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters have been roughly mixed up

parts.note: brass is northern British slang for money

explanation.surface: An unpleasant layabout had cash and grew insolent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' rearranges SLOBAD (from slob 'ad) to BOLDAS; BRASS is northern English slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold as brass is an idiom for impudent and shameless, very cheeky.

clue.text: See 20
Appearing in cinema, the new goddess

indicators.note: appearing in says the word is found within the following words

explanation.surface: A new goddess turns up on the big screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, also Athena, is the Greek goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: Particular sort of craft? You need to purchase lots of paper, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks that the phrase is to be pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: to buy a ream, a large quantity of paper

explanation.surface: A craft hobby that needs plenty of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear': 'buy ream' is pronounced like the answer. 'Craft' misleads towards handicrafts; it means a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme is an ancient galley with two banks of oars, a kind of seagoing vessel.

clue.text: Lord reportedly unable to have children?

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a baron is a lord, a member of the peerage

explanation.surface: A nobleman is said to be infertile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly': BARON is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren means infertile, incapable of producing offspring.

clue.text: Defendant gives this reply, but later falls apart

indicators.note: falls apart says the letters break up and re-form

explanation.surface: A defendant replies in court, but his case later collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls apart' rearranges BUT LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a defendant's answer in legal pleading, a contradicting reply.

clue.text: This queen would be overthrown in a republic in Africa

indicators.note: overthrown means turned upside down, so in a down light or here the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Niger is a republic in West Africa

explanation.surface: A queen who would be toppled in an African republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would be overthrown' turns A NIGER backwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is Latin for queen, used in titles and in legal cases.

clue.text: See 11
Loves a party before short break

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a rest is a break

explanation.surface: Someone loves a party before a brief holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the final T of REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Adores is a stronger synonym for loves, as in to adore a person.

clue.text: Protection for a nob

parts.note: nob looks like a toff, but it is slang for the head, so this is something worn to protect the head

explanation.definitionFit: Headgear is anything worn on the head, including helmets that protect the head.

clue.text: Paddy is moderate

definitions.meaning: a paddy is British slang for a fit of rage
to moderate is to soften or tone down

explanation.definitionFit: Temper means both a fit of anger and, as a verb, to tone down or soften.

clue.text: Fish? Someone working in a hospital eats tons

indicators.note: eats means taking something inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a surgeon works in a hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital worker who eats tons of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' puts T inside SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish, the source of caviar.
